'''Felix Ruvimovich Gantmacher''' ({{langx|ru|Феликс Рувимович Гантмахер}}) (23 February 1908 – 16 May 1964) was a [[USSR|Soviet]] [[mathematician]], professor at [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]], well known for his contributions in mechanics, [[linear algebra]] and [[Lie group]] theory. In 1925–1926 he participated in seminar guided by [[Nikolai Chebotaryov]] in Odessa and wrote his first research paper in 1926.

His book ''Theory of Matrices'' (1953) is a standard reference of linear algebra. It has been translated into various languages including a two-volume version in English prepared by [[Joel Lee Brenner]], Donald W. Bushaw, and S. Evanusa.<ref name="Gantmacher1">{{citation |  title=Theory of matrices | year=1959 | first1=Felix | last1=Gantmacher | publisher = AMS Chelsea publishing| author1-link=Felix Gantmacher}}</ref><ref name="Gantmacher2">{{citation |  title=Applications of the theory of matrices | year=1959 | first1=Felix | last1=Gantmacher | publisher = Interscience publishers| author1-link=Felix Gantmacher |url = https://books.google.com/books?id=cyX32q8ZP5cC&pg=PA53 | isbn=9780821826645 }}</ref> [[George Herbert Weiss]] noted that "this book cannot be recommended too highly as it contains material otherwise unavailable in book form".<ref>{{cite journal |first=George |last=Weiss |year=1960 |title=Review of ''Applications of the Theory of Matrices'' |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |volume=131 |issue=3398 |pages=405–6 |doi=10.1126/science.131.3398.405-a |s2cid=120423210 }}</ref>

Gantmacher collaborated with [[Mark Krein]] on ''Oscillation Matrices and Kernels and Small Vibrations of Mechanical Systems''.<ref name="GantmacherKrein">{{citation |  title=Oscillation Matrices and Kernels and Small Vibrations of Mechanical Systems: Revised Edition | year=2002 | first1=Felix | last1=Gantmacher
| first2=Mark | last2=Krein | publisher = AMS Chelsea Publishing| author1-link=Felix Gantmacher| author2-link=Mark Krein|
url = https://www.ams.org/bookstore-getitem/item=CHEL-345-H}}</ref>

In 1939 he contributed to the classification problem of the real [[Lie algebra]]s.<ref name="GantmacherLie1">{{citation |  title=On the classification of real simple Lie groups | year=1939 | first1=Felix | last1=Gantmacher
|  publisher = AMS Chelsea Publishing| author1-link=Felix Gantmacher|  journal=[[Sbornik: Mathematics]]| volume = 5(47)| issue = 2| pages = 217–250|
url = http://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sm&paperid=5777&what=fullt&option_lang=rus}}</ref>

In the same year he wrote on [[automorphism]]s of [[complex Lie group]]s.<ref name="GantmacherLie2">{{citation |  title=Canonical representation of automorphisms of a complex semi-simple Lie group | year=1939 | first1=Felix | last1=Gantmacher
|  publisher = AMS Chelsea Publishing| author1-link=Felix Gantmacher|  journal=[[Sbornik: Mathematics]]| volume = 5(47)| issue = 2| pages = 101–146|url = http://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sm&paperid=5771&what=fullt&option_lang=rus
}}</ref>

His son [[Vsevolod Gantmakher|Vsevolod Gantmacher]] was a noted physicist.
